subject: Post-demo: performance qualification + multi-region residency checklist
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Reynolds <areynolds@finovate.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: performance qualification + multi-region residency checklist

Alex — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick post-call recap and a few clarifying questions so we can size the right environment and provide an accurate pricing/rollout plan. I put the items we need below and attached our product datasheet for reference.

Summary from call
- Primary use case: real-time agent assist and customer-facing chat in the Finovate web app. Partial streaming required for low-latency token updates to the UI.
- Expected steady-state peak: ~200 concurrent users during peak day; company expects bursts to 450 concurrent for short windows.
- Token mix estimate: 40 tokens in prompt, 120 tokens generated average per request.
- Regions: US & EU required for production; APAC considered for Q2 2027. EU data must remain in-region for regulated product flows.

Clarifying questions (action items for Finovate)
1) Latency targets: Can you confirm p95 latency goals for each region? We heard approx 100-150ms but want explicit numbers (US/EU/APAC).
2) Concurrency vs throughput: Is the concurrent user number the correct sizing signal, or do you prefer estimated requests/sec at peak?
3) Streaming: You confirmed partial token streaming is required for the agent UI. Is there any fallback to non-streaming for low-bandwidth clients?
4) Data residency: Which datasets require EU residency only (logs, telemetry, vector DB)? Any retention limits we should know about?
5) Security/compliance: Do you need a Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment in EU from day one or would a dedicated-hosted EU region with contractual controls be acceptable?

Next steps from Redwood
- We will circulate a proposed test plan and perf-run slots (30 minute windows) for November 23-25.
- Monica will draft a Dedicated capacity estimate for EU and a Hosted + Dedicated hybrid for US.
- We will provision a short-lived test cluster for a perf run once we get the sample workload CSV attached by you.

Attachments: redwood-performance-datasheet.pdf (overview), sample perf plan (placeholder), network-trace-sample.txt

Thanks — feel free to reply inline.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---
Redwood Inference | developer-first inference runtime
From: Alex Reynolds <areynolds@finovate.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
Cc: Marissa Dunn <marissa.dunn@finovate.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: performance qualification + multi-region residency checklist

Jordan — great recap, thanks. Answers inline below.

1) Latency targets: p95 targets we are comfortable with for production: US 120ms, EU 140ms, APAC 200ms. We understand APAC is tougher; 200ms is our initial threshold.
2) Concurrency vs throughput: We usually size off concurrent connected users plus average request/sec. For planning use: 220 concurrent steady, 480 burst, avg 3 reqs/user/hour, peak estimated 200 rps sustained for 5-10 minutes.
3) Streaming: streaming required in all regions. We do not plan to fall back to non-streaming for the agent UI. Mobile clients may need a low-bandwidth mode — we will flag those later.
4) Data residency: Vector DB and PII-derived telemetry must stay in-region for EU flows. Application logs can cross-region if anonymized; retention policy for EU personal data is 90 days.
5) Deployment model: For EU-regulated flows we will need Private or customer-dedicated control plane in EU. For US, hosted Redwood with contractual controls is fine for now.

Perf test window: Nov 24 at 10:00 - 11:00 PT would work for us. We will attach a sample workload CSV after this thread.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Reynolds
Director of Product, Finovate
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-15T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: performance qualification + multi-region residency checklist (Finovate)

Monica/Vivek — forwarding Alexs answers. Key asks: EU must be private/dedicated for regulated flows; streaming required; p95 targets: US 120ms, EU 140ms, APAC 200ms; concurrency steady 220, burst to 480, peak ~200 rps.

Immediate requests for our team
- Monica: please draft cost estimate for two options: (A) Dedicated EU private deployment + Hosted US; (B) Dedicated EU + Dedicated APAC + Hosted US (APAC for Q2 rollout). Include a 12-month commit and monthly OPEX.
- Vivek: can we provision a 1-node test cluster in eu-west-1 with streaming-enabled model variant and token-burst throttles for Nov 24 10:00 PT perf run? Need guidance on expected instance type and concurrency caps to hit ~200 rps.
- Both: prepare a short runbook for the perf window (data to collect: p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, network RTTs, KV cache hit rates).

Attachments: finovate-workload-sample.csv (placeholder — customer will send their final)

I will confirm back to Alex with the slots and attach the perf plan once you both OK.

-Jordan
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-16T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo: performance qualification + multi-region residency checklist (Finovate)

Jordan — confirmed. We can stand up a temporary eu-west-1 test cluster and reserve the Nov 24 10:00 PT slot. Vivek and I will scope instance sizing; preliminary recommendation: 2 x A10G-class nodes with 16 concurrent streams per node to start, tuning after the first run.

Items I need from Finovate before provisioning:
- Final workload CSV (format they shared in the original doc is fine). If they include a sample of streaming vs non-streaming calls, please ask them to mark that column.
- Confirmation on whether vector DB traffic must not egress the EU VPC (they stated yes).

I will prepare the cost comparison doc and drop the link to the HubSpot opportunity once ready. Leaving a short checklist below for our prep.

Prep checklist
- Perf run playbook (J/k)
- Monitoring dashboards: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU util, network RTT, KV cache hit
- Data residency verification steps and log retention config
- Post-run summary template for the customer

Attachments added: network-trace-sample.txt (for troubleshooting), redwood-performance-datasheet.pdf

Monica
